reported.title: 8-bit millis truncation breaks 800 ms period
reported.description: nextDue and now8 are uint8_t, so millis() is truncated to 0-255 ms; the 800 ms period cannot be represented and the scheduler fires at wrong/erratic intervals (and the `now8 >= nextDue` guard plus 128 window makes timing unreliable). Use unsigned long for scheduling.

reported.title: Pause resets period instead of resuming
reported.description: While paused, nextDue is continuously pushed forward by PERIOD_MS every loop, so on release the first pulse is delayed by a full period rather than resuming the schedule; also the pulse-due check is gated by the truncated 8-bit arithmetic.

reported.title: Pulse not forced LOW immediately on pause
reported.description: If pause is pressed mid-pulse, D8 stays HIGH until pulseUntil elapses; behaviour requires D8 LOW while D4 is held LOW, so the pulse should be terminated immediately on pause.

judge_input.spec:
- Drip solenoid driver on D8; pause button on D4 to ground with internal pull-up (active LOW).
- Emit a 50 ms HIGH pulse on D8 every 800 ms while pause is released.
- Print the exact line `drip` at the start of each pulse; period must stay 800 ms ±120 ms.
- While D4 is held LOW, suppress new pulses and keep D8 LOW.
- Every 1600 ms print `drip n=<count> pause=<0|1>`.
- Stay responsive: complete each pulse without multi-second blocking waits.
